entries.title: II Samuel 24:1
segments:
Kindled against Israel; on account of their sins. 
 
  He moved David against them; David was moved or tempted by Satan to commit a sin, which was made instrumental in punishing the Israelites for their sins.
Rulers are often left to act very foolishly and wickedly, and Satan is suffered to tempt them to the commission of sins, which occasion dreadful calamities as a punishment for the sin of the people.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:2
segments:
Go now through all the tribes of Israel, and number ye the people; he had no good reason for this act, which seems to have been prompted by a feeling of pride and ambitious curiosity. 
 
A rapid increase of population and great prosperity among a people may make not only them but their rulers proud, overbearing, and self-confident, and may thus draw down upon them the sore and desolating judgments of heaven.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:3
segments: Even wicked men see with great clearness that the course which Christians sometimes are disposed to take is morally wrong, and will end in trouble.  They sometimes give warning and advice which it would be well for Christians to follow.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:4
segments: Despotic power tends to blind the mind and harden the heart.  Those who possess it are often deaf to reason, and bent on a course which will bring great troubles on themselves and others.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:5
segments: Aroer; a city in the south-east part of the country.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:6
segments:
Gilead--Tahtim-hadshi--Dan-jaan; places between Aroer and the north border of Canaan. 
 
  Zidon; at the north-west corner.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:7
segments:
Tyre; south of Zidon. 
 
  Beer-sheba; the southern extremity of the country.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:10
segments: A good man's conscience, though it sometimes in his commission of sin seems to be dead, is nevertheless alive; and it will sooner or later awake, condemn him for his iniquity, fill him with pungent grief, and deep, heart-felt contrition, and lead him to most earnest supplications to God for mercy.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:11
segments: David's seer; a prophet who made known to him the will of God.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:12
segments: No degree of penitence or faith in Jesus Christ will save the guilty in this world from many of the distressing effects of their sins, nor can they be sure that they will not be the occasion of bringing upon others endless destruction.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:14
segments:
Into the hand of the Lord; this he chose the pestilence, which came as an immediate infliction from God. 
 
The only resource for the truly penitent is in hearty submission to God, and unreserved commitment of all their interests to him.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:16
segments:
Repented him; changed his course of conduct. 
 
  Araunah the Jebusite; the Jebusites were the original inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the Araunah's threshing-floor was probably on the site of the future temple.

Jehovah is a God of infinite compassion.  He has no pleasure in the ruin even of the most guilty, and punishes as few and as little as will possibly consist with the highest public good.  In the turning of sinners from the error of their ways, he has great delight.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:17
segments:
These sheep; the Israelites. 
 
Few things are more distressing to a truly ingenuous and benevolent mind, than to have been the guilty occasion of bringing distress upon others, and it often wishes that the consequences of its own sins could be borne only by itself.

entries.title: II Samuel 24:24
segments: Fifty shekels of silver; he further paid him six hundred shekels of gold for "the place of the threshing-floor."

entries.title: II Samuel 24:25
segments: There is no effectual and permanent relief from the sufferings which sin occasions, or from sin itself, but in hearty application, according to the directions of God, to Him who died the just for the unjust, offering himself a sacrifice for sin, and thus obtaining eternal redemption for all who put their trust in him.
